"own_initiative": work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up; it waits as a proposal card until the user starts it; never for a task the user's message tells you to do. Required unless proposal_id is set.

proposal_id.description: Start a proposal the user told you to start, exactly as proposed: its task_id and nothing else (wake_when_done may accompany a local one). To change it, dismiss_task it and start a new session.

title.description: Under 60 chars; names the task. Shown on the row or card. Required unless proposal_id is set.

prompt.description: The brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like. Required for "user_asked" and "own_initiative" — the call is refused without it, and `background` does not stand in for it; an "offer" leaves it out (the card shows the user's own message) and you send it with proposal_id once they choose New session.

context.description: "fresh" (default) or "fork" — see the tool description. A "fork" from a worktree session gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip (commit first; uncommitted edits stay here); from a plain checkout it shares the folder.

background.description: Required with "fresh", besides `prompt`: at least 80 characters of overall goal, decisions and constraints so far, how this piece fits — for someone who has not seen this conversation. Ignored for "fork".

wake_when_done.description: Once this session (and any sibling still working) ends its turn, or fails to start (unless it waits at a prompt the user answers there, its folder was never opened in Claude Desktop, or the user started, stopped or archived it), and you are idle, the app continues you, whether or not this is set. true also continues you if this session never gets its task some other way, such as a brief that is not sent; default false; not with own_initiative; ignored with target "cloud", which never continues you.

name.description: Optional short handle for the session ([a-z0-9-], ≤24), e.g. "cli-cleanup". Linked sessions and plan steps refer to it by this name; derived from the title when omitted.

use_worktree.description: "fresh" only (rejected with "fork"). false = shares this session's checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session: its worktree, branch and PR, so never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); not accepted from a session set up to move from the user's checkout into a worktree with EnterWorktree (before or after it moves), one working in a worktree on an SSH host, or one whose worktree was given back. At another place named by `cwd`, `host` or `preset`, false = that folder as it is. true = its own git worktree. Omitted: the same folder when this session works in a plain folder and has never had a worktree (its own, a shared one, or one it will enter later); otherwise its own worktree. Omitted with `preset` or `host`, or with `cwd` from a session on an SSH host: the default set on that preset or SSH connection instead.

model.description: "fresh" only, optional: a cheaper model id for mechanical or read-only pieces (e.g. a Sonnet or Haiku id). Same family or cheaper than yours; anything higher is ignored. Omit to inherit yours.

target.description: "fresh" only. "local" (default) = where this session runs. "cloud" = run it as a cloud session (keeps going when this computer sleeps). Needs the repository on GitHub and a cloud environment — the app checks and tells the user if it cannot, and the task then stays as a card for them to start. It starts from this session's pushed branch when it runs in a worktree, else the repository's default branch. model/effort/use_worktree/cwd/source_branch do not apply. Only when the user asks for the cloud. "ssh" = on the SSH connection named by host (or by a preset).

host.description: With target "ssh": the name of one of the user's saved SSH connections (as list_start_targets reports it) — never a raw hostname, user or key. The app connects as the user configured it and may ask them to sign in.

cwd.description: The folder the session works in, when it is not this project: an absolute (or ~/) path on the host it will run on — this computer, this session's host, or the SSH connection named by host (default there: the connection's folder). Must exist; if the user has not trusted it yet the app asks them first. "fresh" only.

environment.description: With target "cloud": the name or id of one of the user's cloud environments (list_start_targets lists them); omitted = the default one. Self-hosted environments and runner pools need the user's own click and are refused, and so is an environment that cannot run this project's repository.

source_branch.description: The existing local branch the new worktree is cut from. Default in this project: this session's base branch (the one picked when it started, or the one its worktree was cut from). If the session has none and either it runs on an SSH host or its project folder is itself a git worktree or submodule, the folder's current commit. Otherwise, the repository's default branch, or the folder's current commit if that is unknown. Only for a session that gets its own worktree (use_worktree true, or the place's default); not with target "cloud".

branch_name.description: A short slug for the new worktree's branch (the app adds the user's branch prefix and a suffix). Only with a worktree.

preset.description: The name of one of the user's saved session presets on this computer: it names the place itself (a folder here or an SSH connection and folder — do not pass host or cwd with it) and brings model, effort and worktree defaults plus its saved environment variables; use_worktree/model/effort override those. Cloud and Remote Control presets are not available here.

effort.description: "fresh" only, optional: reasoning effort at or below yours. Omit to inherit.

permission_mode.description: Optional, local starts only: the permission mode it starts in — this session's own or a lower one (omit to inherit it). A higher mode, or one the app does not offer here, is refused; raising a session is set_session_permission_mode's card to show.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work: the user follows your progress by it and will never ask for it, so it is part of the task. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: propose it and call this.

The result says which case below applies. When the box shows your question, it ends your turn: write no text after this call, since the recap and question say what the user needs and your work above holds the detail. Otherwise your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, with any question the box did not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

1	// Package trailers provides parsing and formatting for Entire commit message trailers.
2	// Trailers are key-value metadata appended to git commit messages following the
3	// git trailer convention (key: value format after a blank line).
4	package trailers
5	
6	import (
7		"fmt"
8		"regexp"
9		"slices"
10		"strings"
11	
12		checkpointID "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/id"
13	)
14	
15	// Trailer key constants used in commit messages.
16	const (
17		// MetadataTrailerKey points to the metadata directory within a commit tree.
18		MetadataTrailerKey = "Entire-Metadata"
19	
20		// StrategyTrailerKey indicates which strategy created the commit.
21		StrategyTrailerKey = "Entire-Strategy"
22	
23		// SessionTrailerKey identifies which session created a commit.
24		SessionTrailerKey = "Entire-Session"
25	
26		// CheckpointTrailerKey links commits to their checkpoint metadata on entire/checkpoints/v1.
27		// Format: a checkpoint ID — either a legacy 12-hex ID (e.g. "a3b2c4d5e6f7")
28		// or a 26-char ULID (see checkpoint/id.CheckpointPattern).
29		// This trailer survives git amend and rebase operations.
30		CheckpointTrailerKey = "Entire-Checkpoint"
31	
32		// AgentTrailerKey identifies the agent that created a checkpoint.
33		// Format: human-readable agent name e.g. "Claude Code", "Cursor"
34		AgentTrailerKey = "Entire-Agent"
35	
36		// OPFAppliedTrailerKey marks an entire/checkpoints/v1 commit whose blobs
37		// have been redacted by the OpenAI Privacy Filter (the opt-in 9th,
38		// network-backed layer, applied on top of the 8 regex layers).
39		// Format: literal "true"; the trailer is omitted entirely when OPF was
40		// not applied. The pre-push rewrite path treats commits lacking this
41		// trailer as candidates to OPF-redact before they reach the remote.
42		OPFAppliedTrailerKey = "Entire-OPF-Applied"
43	
44		// OPFAppliedTrailerValue is the only value that means "OPF ran." Any
45		// other value (or trailer absence) is treated as "not applied" so a
46		// future "false" / "skipped" value never accidentally enables OPF.
47		OPFAppliedTrailerValue = "true"
48	)
49	
50	// Pre-compiled regexes for trailer parsing.
51	var (
52		metadataTrailerRegex   = regexp.MustCompile(MetadataTrailerKey + `:\s*(.+)`)
53		sessionTrailerRegex    = regexp.MustCompile(SessionTrailerKey + `:\s*(.+)`)
54		checkpointTrailerRegex = regexp.MustCompile(CheckpointTrailerKey + `:\s*(` + checkpointID.CheckpointPattern + `)(?:\s|$)`)
55	)
56	
57	// ParseMetadata extracts metadata dir from commit message.
58	// Returns the metadata directory and true if found, empty string and false otherwise.
59	func ParseMetadata(commitMessage string) (string, bool) {
60		matches := metadataTrailerRegex.FindStringSubmatch(commitMessage)
61		if len(matches) > 1 {
62			return strings.TrimSpace(matches[1]), true
63		}
64		return "", false
65	}
66	
67	// ParseSession extracts the session ID from a commit message.
68	// Returns the session ID and true if found, empty string and false otherwise.
69	// Note: If multiple Entire-Session trailers exist, this returns only the first one.
70	func ParseSession(commitMessage string) (string, bool) {
71		matches := sessionTrailerRegex.FindStringSubmatch(commitMessage)
72		if len(matches) > 1 {
73			return strings.TrimSpace(matches[1]), true
74		}
75		return "", false
76	}

**Worth changing (production)**

1. **`cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go:155-161`**: `checkpointFromTrailerLine` re-implements `checkpointTrailerLineRegex` (line 165).
   - The two give the same result for an unindented line, because `NewCheckpointID` checks the same pattern.
   - Cost: the remover (`RemoveCheckpointTrailers`) and the new final-block readers now each have their own definition of "a checkpoint trailer line". If either one is loosened later (key case, spacing), amend could keep a trailer the readers can't see, or the other way round.
   - Use: `checkpointTrailerLineRegex.FindStringSubmatch(line)` then `NewCheckpointID(m[1])`. Alternatively, add one `trailerValue(line, key)` helper and use it here and in `HasOPFApplied` (line 403, which has the same `strings.Cut` shape).

2. **`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:313-328`**: `hasUserContent` copies the comment-dropping loop from the new `trailers.StripEditorComments` (`trailers.go:189-201`). Both use the same `HasPrefix(line, commentPrefix)` test on the untrimmed line, after `CutAtScissors`.
   - Cost: two definitions of "a line git's cleanup drops".
   - Use: `if commentBlock { message = trailers.StripEditorComments(message, commentPrefix) }`. The loop then only has to skip blank lines and trailer lines.

3. **`manual_commit_hooks.go:332-340`**: `lastNonBlankLine` is the same loop as `AutoCommentPrefix` (`trailers.go:234-242`). It also skips the existing `isBlankLine` (`trailers.go:337`), as do the new loops at `trailers.go:374` and `trailers.go:425`.
   - Use: move it into `trailers`, write it with `isBlankLine`, export it, and call it from `AutoCommentPrefix` and from strategy.

4. **`trailers.go:370-381`**: `appendTrailerLine` re-implements the paragraph scan and subject check from `finalTrailerBlock` (lines 419-430). Its own comment says the writer and readers must share one grammar.
   - Cost: two scans that must stay in sync.
   - Use: one shared `finalParagraph(lines) (start, end int, ok bool)` helper. It can't simply call `finalTrailerBlock(trimmed) != nil`, because the two differ when the message ends with a whitespace-only line.

**Worth changing (tests)**

5. **`integration_test/checkpoint_trailer_authority_test.go:373`**: `keepAllTrailers` is identical to `keepAll` in `redo_adversarial_test.go:19`, which is in the same package with the same build tag. Use `keepAll`.

6. **`checkpoint_trailer_authority_test.go:332-346`**: `editorCommit` repeats the first half of `advCommit` (`rewrite_adversarial_test.go:54-71`): stage, write the message file, run `prepareCommitMsgCmd`, read the file back. The same steps are inlined again at lines 118-124, 199-205, 262-268 and 287-293.
   - Use: pull out a `runPrepareCommitMsg(env, message, source) string` helper and call it from `advCommit`, `editorCommit` and those tests.

7. **`cmd/entire/cli/attach_test.go:1958-1969`**: this re-implements `headCommitOf(t)` (`attach_commit_test.go:39`).

8. **`attach_test.go:1890-1897` and `attach_test.go:1976`**: these re-implement `readSummary(t, named.String())` (`attach_commit_test.go:78`).

**Optional or low value**

- **`trailers.go:124-131`**: `ParseCheckpointFromFinalTrailerBlock` could return the first element of `ParseAllCheckpointsFromFinalTrailerBlock`. It is 6 lines with an early return, so leaving it is fine.
- **`manual_commit_hooks.go:827-836`**: `withoutDeletedCheckpoints` now runs twice, so `checkpoint.LoadDeletedCheckpoints` runs twice. Loading the list once and calling `deleted.Contains` would avoid that. This is minor.

**Not worth changing**

- **`gitCommentPrefix` (`manual_commit_hooks.go:2817`) vs `gitConfigValue` (`checkpoint_sync_capture.go:253`)**: the semantics differ. `core.commentChar` and `core.commentString` are aliases where the last one set wins, which needs `--get-regexp` over both keys. Two `--get` calls can't tell which came last, and `gitConfigValue`'s `TrimSpace` would also strip a commentString's whitespace. Running `exec.CommandContext` directly matches the other 28 git calls in strategy, none of which use `gitexec`.
- **`CutAtScissors`/`isScissorsLine` vs the scissors search in `RemoveCheckpointTrailers` (line 261)**: the semantics differ on purpose. `RemoveCheckpointTrailers` doesn't know the comment prefix (its doc says so) and matches with `strings.Contains`. One note for the correctness reviewer: it still treats prose that mentions the marker as a cut, which this PR now says git does not do.
- **`addInheritedCheckpointTrailer` / `addCheckpointTrailerWithComment`**: both search for the first comment-prefix line, but that duplication predates the PR; the PR only adds the prefix parameter. The same goes for the near-identical read, check, add and write blocks in `inheritSquashedCheckpointTrailers` and `inheritReplacedCommitsTrailers`, which the PR edits the same way. They could share a helper, but that is out of this PR's scope.
- **`authorityAgentTurn`, `setRepoGitConfig`, `runCommitMsgHook`, `gitCommentBlock`**: no existing equivalent. Other tests inline these steps.
